sources.text:
Thomas Markle Sr. Indicted on Two Federal Possession Counts in California, Facing up to 40 Years
A federal indictment brings serious criminal allegations against the Duchess of Sussex's estranged father before the US courts
Thomas Markle Sr., the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, has been indicted on two federal counts of possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). A federal grand jury in Los Angeles returned the indictment on Tuesday, 24 November 2026.
According to the US Department of Justice, each count carries a maximum prison term of 20 years. The 82-year-old could face 40 years in prison if convicted on both counts and given consecutive maximum sentences.
The indictment follows Markle's arrest in Florida earlier this month and an FBI investigation into suspected child sexual abuse material recovered from storage facilities in California. Markle has previously denied the allegations. He remains presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
Thomas Markle Sr. Indictment Details FBI Investigation and Arrests
Federal prosecutors allege that Thomas Wayne Markle knowingly possessed film negatives containing child sexual abuse material on 30 October and 4 November 2026.
The indictment alleges that the material was transported through interstate or international commerce. Prosecutors also allege that some of the material involved children under the age of 12.
FBI agents obtained court-authorised warrants to search two storage units in the Los Angeles area, registered to Markle. Authorities said he had rented both units since 2008.
Investigators recovered approximately 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books containing suspected child sexual abuse material. This figure represents the number of items seized, not the number of individual criminal offences.
Markle was initially arrested in Florida on 6 November under a federal criminal complaint containing a single possession count.
First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli described the allegations as 'extremely serious' and pledged to prosecute the case to the fullest extent permitted under federal law.
Markle was subsequently released on home detention with electronic monitoring. He returned to custody on 10 November after an alleged violation of those conditions involving his ankle monitor.
On 19 November, US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Griffin ruled in Florida that Markle was competent to stand trial, based on an independent psychiatric evaluation.
The ruling established his capacity to understand the criminal proceedings and to assist in his defence. It did not determine whether he committed the alleged offences.
Thomas Markle Sr.'s Denial and Meghan Markle's Earlier Response
The American investigation followed allegations of material reportedly found among Markle's belongings in Cebu, the Philippines.
His son, Thomas Markle Jr., claimed in October that he had discovered suspected child sexual abuse material and had subsequently alerted authorities.
Philippine National Police spokesperson Brigadier General Allen Rae Co confirmed that criminal complaints against Markle were filed with prosecutors in Cebu on 16 November.
The complaints concern alleged offences of possession and distribution under Philippine law and are separate from the two federal counts in California.
Markle denied his son's accusations in a Daily Mail interview published on 23 October, calling the allegations 'a bunch of lies'.
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, also addressed the earlier allegations on 23 October, stating she was 'deeply distressed' by the reports.
She explained that her decision to distance herself from her father and to prevent him from having contact with her children was intended to protect them.
Her statement preceded the November arrests and does not constitute a response to the latest federal indictment.
The Justice Department confirmed that Markle remains in federal custody in Florida, and his arraignment is expected in Los Angeles in the coming weeks.
An exact arraignment date was not disclosed in Tuesday's announcement. The FBI investigation is ongoing, and prosecutors must prove Markle's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt to secure a conviction at trial.

The estranged father of Meghan Markle, wife of Britain’s Prince Harry, was indicted by a California grand jury on Tuesday on two counts of possession of images of child sexual abuse.
Thomas Markle, 82, who is already in custody in Florida after removing the ankle monitor that had been attached as a condition of house arrest, is expected to be arraigned in the United States District Court in Los Angeles in the coming weeks.
US indictment and alleged evidence
The indictment alleges that Markle had 35mm negatives showing child sexual abuse, including at least one image involving a prepubescent minor.
Court documents allege Markle had illegal photographs both in the Philippines, where he had previously lived, and in two rented storage facilities in Los Angeles.
Prosecutors say FBI agents seized dozens of images on slides, film negatives and in books, including two that appear to depict Markle with children who are either naked or in various states of undress.
A Florida judge this month ordered that Markle undergo a psychiatric examination after finding “reasonable cause to believe” that he was suffering from a condition “rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense.”
Following this examination by a psychiatrist, Markle was deemed fit to stand trial.
Philippines seeks charges
Philippine authorities filed criminal complaints against Markle last week in Cebu, where he is said to have lived for over a year, regional prosecutor Graeme Elmido has said.
Police recommended that Markle be charged with two counts of distributing child sexual abuse material and one count of possessing such material under Philippine law.
“The complaints will go through preliminary evaluation,” Elmido said.
“If the evidence warrants… a regular preliminary investigation subpoena will then be sent to Markle Sr to answer the charges.”
Markle’s legal troubles began in October when the British tabloid The Sun reported that his son, Thomas Markle Jr, had discovered child sex abuse images while going through boxes found in his father’s former home in the Philippines.
Markle had been living in Cebu until reportedly returning to the United States earlier this year.
Meghan Markle said last month that she was “deeply distressed” by accusations that her father possessed images of child sexual abuse.
She said she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous “troubling and disturbing” allegations.
Harry, the second son of King Charles III and estranged brother of heir to the throne Prince William, married Meghan, an American former actor, at Windsor Castle in May 2018.

sources.text:
- Grand jury indictment returned on Tuesday doubles Los Angeles federal charges to two counts
- Each count carries up to 20 years in prison if convicted, US attorney says
- Judge ruled Markle mentally competent for trial after psychiatric evaluation last week
LOS ANGELES — Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Britain’s Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle, and father-in-law of Britain’s Prince Harry, was indicted on Tuesday in US federal court on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material.
The indictment doubles the number of federal charges currently lodged in Los Angeles against the 82-year-old Markle in a case that grew out of an investigation initiated last month in the Philippines, where he previously resided.
The elder Markle was originally charged on November 5 in a criminal complaint with a single felony count of possessing child sexual abuse images.
According to an FBI affidavit filed with the complaint, the material in question was found in two Los Angeles storage units and included two explicit photos of Markle posed with a naked underage girl and other images of him with children in various stages of undress.
One of the photos showed a naked girl in a room that appeared to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines, the affidavit said.
Philippine police said last week criminal complaints had been filed against Markle in the country’s Cebu province, where he once lived, accusing him of violating local laws against online sexual abuse and exploitation of children.
Markle has denied the allegations, telling the Daily Mail the claims were untrue and describing them as “sick lies.”
He was arrested on November 6 at a Florida assisted-living facility where he has been a patient, and is expected to be transferred to California in the coming weeks to be arraigned in US District Court in Los Angeles on the two-count grand jury indictment returned on Tuesday.
Following a court-ordered psychiatric evaluation of Markle, a US magistrate judge in Tampa, Florida, last week ruled that he was mentally competent to stand trial, meaning that he understood the proceedings against him and could assist in his own defense.
Each count of possession of child sexual abuse material, an offense referred to in the US criminal code as possession of child pornography, is punishable by up to 20 years in prison if he is convicted, the US attorney’s statement said.
Meghan Markle, an American actor, has been estranged from her father since the run-up to her marriage to King Charles’ younger son, Harry, in 2018, when the duchess has said she first became aware of allegations against her father. She has said she was “deeply distressed” over the matter, which led her to cut off contact between her father and her two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5.

sources.news_title: Thomas Markle Indicted On Two Counts Over Alleged Possession Of CSAM Involving Prepubescent Minors
sources.text:
Thomas Markle is facing two federal counts involving the alleged possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) depicting prepubescent minors. The indictment was handed down in California, where the materials were reportedly found in his rented storage units. The development comes after the FBI initially arrested him in Florida in early November, where he is currently jailed.
California Grand Jury Indicts Thomas Markle
On November 24, a federal grand jury in Los Angeles indicted Thomas Markle on two counts of possession of child sex abuse material. According to a press release from the U.S. Attorney’s Office of the Central District of California, the charges involve materials depicting prepubescent minors.
The FBI arrested 82-year-old Markle on November 6 at a senior care facility in Lakeland, Florida, where he was staying. He was initially charged with one federal count of CSAM and was released after his defense argued he was not a flight risk. Days later, however, Markle allegedly cut off his ankle monitor, prompting the magistrate judge to order his immediate arrest and detainment pending further proceedings.
Markle is expected to be transferred to California for his arraignment within the next few weeks.
Images Depict Minors Younger Than 12
Markle’s charges stem from an FBI investigation, in which agents seized 78 items from two California storage units that he had been renting since 2008. The most recent rent payment was made through autopay in October.
Among the pieces of evidence discovered were 35mm film negatives depicting “prepubescent minors and minors who had not yet reached the age of 12 years old,” the press release noted. One other photo showed Markle with a nude girl, while another showed a prepubescent girl in what was identified as a motel room in the Philippines.
Other photos show Markle “with children in various stages of undress.”
- Thomas Markle was deemed fit for trial following his evaluation.
- He said he has “nothing to hide” and maintains his innocence.
- Thomas Markle Sr. reportedly has no money in his commissary account.
- A relative revealed Thomas Markle’s “girls trip” to Asia was an “open family secret.”
- Meghan Markle faced criticism over her silence about Thomas Markle’s scandal.
Thomas Markle Also Faces Complaints In The Philippines
Markle is also facing charges in Cebu, Philippines, where he lived before returning to the U.S. in May.
In October, Thomas Markle Jr. handed over materials and devices he found at his father’s home, prompting an investigation.
On November 16, the Philippine National Police (PNP) stated that they have filed three charges against Markle: one count of possessing Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Material (CSAEM) and two counts of offering, distributing, selling, exporting, or importing any form of CSAEM, as reported by ITV.
Prosecutors will decide whether to formally file a case. “A regular preliminary investigation subpoena will then be sent to Markle Sr. to answer the charges” if the case proceeds, a regional prosecutor said.
His Storage Unit In Mexico Was Also Raided
On November 2, authorities also raided Markle’s storage unit in Rosarito, Baja California, Mexico. It was located near his retirement home, where he lived for more than a decade before relocating to the Philippines in 2025.
The Daily Mail reported that authorities seized several items, including magazines, VHS tapes, thumb drives, and a computer. The storage unit was rented sometime in 2017, but reports noted that he stopped making payments in 2024. His items, however, remained locked until the raid. Per the search warrant, Guardia Nacional officers were authorized to find “evidence consisting of child sexual abuse material.”
No formal charges have been filed against Markle in Mexico, but the investigation remains active.
Thomas Markle Maintains His Innocence
Markle has vehemently denied the allegations and maintained his innocence throughout the controversy. His estranged daughter, Meghan, issued a statement in October, saying she was “deeply distressed.” Meghan’s half-brother, Thomas Jr., also said that he no longer wants anything to do with his father. “I won’t speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him,” he said.
Among his three children, the only one standing in Markle’s corner is Samantha, who believes his brother is “trying to get revenge” on their father, per The Blast.
Markle’s transfer date from Florida to California has not been announced. He remains in custody at the Pinellas County Jail in the meantime.
